text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The European Union wants an urgent solution to the Cyprus issue. Nicosia does not believe it is on a collision course with the bloc.
- Trade unions find it difficult to follow the same line on President Glafcos Clerides' proposal to modify cost of living allowances.
- Greece warns the European Union over Cyprus. Move to include the Turkish Cypriots in talks will hit union's growth.
- Denktash Jr adds voice to threats on opening up the fenced-in town of Varosha.
- Cyprus may buy Iraqi crude at $19 per barrel.
- Hellenic Bank Offshore Department in Limassol gets an ISO 9002 quality standards certification.
- Cyprus and Armenia push for a deal to avoid double taxation.
- Europe mounts its pressure on Cyprus.
- Powerful European states aim at changing the accession deal to include Turkish Cypriots in process.
- Doctors in the civil service threaten a 24-hour strike to push demands.
- Right-wing Disy chairman Yiannakis Matsis disagrees with his deputy Nicos Anastassiades on the timing of party elections.
- Britain and the United States attempt to link the solution of the Cyprus problem to EU accession.
